title: Bank exit & account closure
summary: Leaving Singapore or losing your EP — sequence SGD account closure, PayNow / GIRO teardown, tax-refund rails, and residual standing instructions so money does not get trapped after you fly.

sections.title: Decide: keep a SGD rail vs full closure
sections.body: If IRAS may still owe you a tax refund, an employer may pay a final tranche, or you might return within months, keeping one multi-currency or SGD account can be cheaper than remitting twice. Full exit (no return plans, no local income) usually means orderly closure. Do not leave dormant accounts with forgotten GIRO pulls.
bullets: Keep one account if IR21 / tax refund / final salary is still pending
Full exit → inventory every SGD product before you book the last flight
Between-jobs stay: do not close the account you need for rent while STVP runs — see /journeys/between-jobs

sections.title: Inventory PayNow, GIRO, cards, and standing instructions
sections.body: Banks will not magically cancel every autopay when you close. List PayNow proxies (NRIC/FIN, mobile, UEN links), GIRO to SP Utilities / telecom / condo MCST, credit-card autopay, and investment platforms that debit SGD. Tear those down first so closure is not blocked by open mandates.
bullets: Screenshot PayNow registration and deregister mobile / FIN proxies you will lose
Cancel GIRO at the biller and confirm the bank mandate is dead
Destroy or securely store physical cards; freeze digital wallets tied to the account

sections.title: Pass expiry and bank KYC clocks
sections.body: When an EP or FIN status changes, banks re-run KYC. Some freeze online banking or reject remittances until you update pass documents — or until you close. Bring the cancellation letter / STVP email / new IPA if you are staying. Do not assume Singpass login alone keeps the account fully usable after pass cancel.
bullets: Update residential address and pass documents before the FIN looks stale in the bank’s file
Ask whether the account can stay open on STVP / new EP, or must close
Export 12–24 months of statements while e-banking still works

sections.title: Remit residual SGD, then close
sections.body: Leave a small buffer for unexpected GIRO retries, then remitting the rest. Confirm FX cut-offs and whether the bank requires branch attendance for foreign beneficiaries. After the final outward remittance clears, submit the closure request and ask for a written confirmation letter for your tax / visa files.
bullets: Keep a buffer for one utility cycle after you think everything is cancelled
Prefer account-to-account remittance over carrying cash through Changi
File the closure confirmation with IR21 / exit paperwork

sections.title: Joint accounts and dependant access
sections.body: Joint SGD accounts and dependant supplementary cards often outlive the main EP holder’s mental model of “we’re leaving.” Remove supplementary cards, change signatories, or close joint products deliberately — especially if a spouse remains on DP/LOC while you exit.
bullets: Map every joint holder and supplementary card before closure day
If family stays, decide who remains the primary banked adult in Singapore
Do not strand school or helper GIRO on an account you are closing

sections.title: Cash timing vs furniture storage
sections.body: Bank closure week often collides with movers and temporary storage invoices billed in SGD. Keep enough local balance to clear storage and utility final bills, or pre-pay with a card that will still work abroad. Sketch storage months before you drain the account.
bullets: Use /tools/storage-months for a rough SGD storage float
Pay the final SP / telecom bills before the account dies
Leaving playbook still owns shipping and deposit recovery sequencing
